description: We're a driven team competing in NASA Space Apps, mixing skills in software dev, cybersecurity, and problem-solving. We want to build a solid, useful solution to our challenge — not just a demo.
summary:
Testing lunar and Martian hardware on Earth is vital, but no single terrestrial site replicates extreme extraterrestrial environments: polar ice sheets lack volcanic basalt, while rocky deserts lack cryogenic cold traps. Historically, analog testing sites were chosen through subjective habit rather than empirical fidelity, risking undetected hardware failures during surface missions.
We developed SubZero, an open-access decision-support platform and multi-site portfolio optimizer for Artemis Lunar South Pole and Mars exploration. Ingesting satellite observations from NASA SRTM, NASA CERES/POWER, and ERA5, SubZero evaluates global candidate sites across 8 physical planetary criteria calibrated against NASA LRO Diviner and Curiosity REMS ground truth.
To overcome single-site limitations, SubZero implements submodular greedy optimization to identify complementary 2-to-3 site test portfolios that maximize condition coverage and eliminate critical test blind spots. It further validates ranking robustness using 1,000 Dirichlet Monte Carlo perturbation trials.
SubZero replaces guesswork with reproducible science—de-risking multi-billion-dollar space missions, protecting flight payloads, and saving space agencies millions in redundant expedition costs.
details: SubZero is an empirical decision-support platform and multi-site portfolio optimizer built with Python 3.13 and Streamlit that quantitatively evaluates and selects Earth-based testing grounds for Artemis Lunar South Pole and Mars surface exploration. It scores 15 global candidate sites across 8 physical planetary criteria—including terrain slope roughness, cryogenic deep-freeze, UV radiation flux, regolith composition, diurnal temperature swings, atmospheric pressure, aridity, and polar grazing illumination—by ingesting 30m digital elevation models from NASA SRTM and ASTER GDEM, satellite solar and UV radiometry from NASA CERES/POWER, and 40 years of ECMWF ERA5 climate reanalysis, all calibrated directly against ground-truth mission observations from NASA LRO (Diviner, LOLA, CRaTER) and the Curiosity rover (REMS and MOLA). Recognizing the fundamental challenge that no single Earth location replicates all extraterrestrial conditions (polar ice caps lack basaltic regolith while volcanic deserts lack cryogenic cold traps), SubZero’s core innovation is a submodular greedy coverage optimizer that algorithmically pairs complementary 2-to-3 site test portfolios to eliminate hardware testing blind spots without costly redundant expeditions. To ensure scientific rigor and eliminate human subjectivity, the engine features 1,000-run Dirichlet Monte Carlo perturbation trials to verify ranking stability, automated detection of statistical ties within 2%, interactive Plotly dual-radar profile comparisons, and responsive Folium geospatial mapping. Developed with an open-source data science stack (NumPy, SciPy, Pandas, Folium, and Plotly) and validated with an 18-test automated suite matching NASA's 75.50 worked example, our team thoughtfully separated scientific physical fidelity from travel logistics while accounting for sensor rain shadows, delivering an accessible, open-science tool that de-risks multi-billion-dollar planetary missions, protects flight hardware from catastrophic failure, and saves space agencies millions in expedition budgets.
